title: The Vail Kiln-house — the roof over the boy, Low Kiln, Sill
caption: The house known by its objects before its people, drawn at the scale of a basket set just inside the door: the boy's room with its bed, one crust in the fold and four nails, four and a knot overhead; the other room with the carried fire under ash at four and a gap, the loaf shelf with two unnamed gaps and the charcoal beneath unread, the clay jar, the charred slate and the clean dark line beside the finer grey called the thaw. Beyond it the kiln at its mouth, the wheel-shed with the cold damper of two bites, the Debt Loft and the finger's-width-open back room, the drying racks, the flagstones with the bright patch, the yard well with its bare trough and the Clay Road going west to the Cross and east to Greybank. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the month of Ember.
